seo.description: Visit the kasbah of Taroudant: the quieter former royal quarter in the north-east of the medina, square towers and a different pace from the main souks.
seo.og_description: Explore the kasbah district of Taroudant — quieter lanes, fortification character and local life in the Little Marrakech.

name: The Kasbah
hero_subtitle: The former royal quarter of Taroudant: quieter lanes, square towers and a slower pace than the main souks.

overview.title: A quieter historic quarter
overview.p1: The kasbah of Taroudant sits in the north-east of the walled medina. Historically tied to power and defence, it is now a residential and atmospheric quarter.
overview.p2: Walking here pairs well with Bab el-Kasbah, the most ornate gate of the ramparts.
overview.p3: Public streets are free. Respect private doorways and ask before photographing people at close range.

q1.question: Is The Kasbah free to visit?
q1.answer: In most cases public areas are free. Confirm any ticketed interiors on site.

q2.question: How long should I spend?
q2.answer: Thirty minutes to two hours depending on the site and your pace.

q3.question: What is the best time to go?
q3.answer: Morning or late afternoon for cooler temperatures and better light.

q4.question: How do I get there from the medina?
q4.answer: On foot if central, or by petit taxi. Ask for the place name as a landmark.

q5.question: Can I take photos?
q5.answer: Usually yes outdoors. Ask before photographing people or restricted interiors.
